There is no form and no inbox here. One phone number, answered by an automated assistant at any hour, puts you through to an independent pool service company in the Tucson area.

What to say when the assistant answers

The assistant only needs a quick picture of the problem. A few plain details let the pool company know what it is walking into before it says hello.

  • What you are seeing: green or cloudy water, a pump that hums or stays silent, a water level that keeps dropping, white crust on the tile, a light that will not turn on.
  • When it started, and anything that happened just before, such as a monsoon storm, a power outage or a party.
  • Where the pool is: the town or neighborhood, for example Oro Valley, Rita Ranch, Sahuarita or near Tanque Verde, and a nearby cross street if you like.
  • Whether you are after regular visits, a single cleanup or a fix.
  • The best number for a call back, and good times to reach you.

You do not need to know the name of a part or what is wrong. Describing what you see and hear is enough.

If the pool company cannot pick up

Sometimes the company is on another call or out at a pool. In that case the assistant notes your name, callback number and area, plus a short note on what the pool is doing, and hands all of that over for a return call. The line cannot tell you exactly when that will happen. Keep your phone nearby and answer unfamiliar numbers for a while, because the call back may not come from (520) 372-1083.

Once you are talking with the company, everything from there is between the two of you: the visit, the diagnosis, the quote, the work and the bill. Before repair or equipment work, get the company's license number and search it in the Registrar of Contractors' public license lookup. Nobody at the line checks that for you.

Call someone else first in an emergency

Smell gas at the pool heater

Leave the area at once and keep others away. Do not touch the heater, switches or anything that could spark. Once you are clear, dial 911, then the Southwest Gas leak line at 877-860-6020.

Someone is hurt or in the water

Call 911 right away. A pool line is never the right number for a medical emergency or a child in trouble in the water.

Sparks, shocks or a burning smell

Keep everyone out of the water and away from the equipment. If you can reach the breaker safely, switch the pool circuit off. Electrical repairs are work for a professional.

Everything else pool related

For problems that are not an emergency, call the line. A green pool, a stopped pump or a slow leak can wait the few minutes it takes to reach a local company.

What happens to the details you give

The automated assistant may record or log what you say on the call, for example your name and number, your part of town and the trouble you describe, so that it can be handed to the pool business that takes your call. The privacy policy explains how the line and this website are designed to handle information, and the terms of use set out what the line is and is not responsible for.

The line can be paid a referral fee by the companies. That never changes the fact that the call itself is free to you.

Where the line takes calls from

Call from anywhere in Tucson and the nearby communities of Pima County: the city itself, from the east side out toward Rita Ranch, plus Oro Valley, the Catalina Foothills, Marana, Vail, Sahuarita and Green Valley. Each town page covers local water, weather and rules worth knowing.

Common questions

Can I email Tucson Pool Cleaning Pro or fill out a form?

No. The line works by phone only, so there is no email address or contact form. A call gets your problem in front of a local pool company quickly, or gets your details to it for a call back.

What time can I call the pool line?

Whenever you need to. The automated assistant picks up around the clock, every day of the year. Visit times are up to the pool business itself.

What if I miss the pool company's call back?

Call the company back on the number it called from, since the job is between you and that company. If you cannot reach it, you can ring the line again and explain that you are waiting on a return call.

Who do I contact about a problem with work that was already done?

Start with the pool business that handled the job, since the agreement was with it. If a licensed contractor did the work and the two of you cannot sort it out, the Arizona Registrar of Contractors accepts homeowner complaints online, and its lookup lists each license's record.

Does calling the line commit me to anything?

No. The call is free and you are not agreeing to hire anyone. Listen to what the pool company finds and what it would charge, and then decide.

Ready when you are, day or night

It is one free call, day or night. Tell the assistant what the pool is doing and which part of the Tucson area it is in, and you are transferred to a local, independently owned pool company that looks at the pool in person and names its own price.
